test_title: PYST 68: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Three years ago, the age of a person was six times the age of his younger brother. Eight years later, the age of the person will be three years less than twice the age of his younger brother. Find the present ages of the person and his younger brother.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For age-based questions, verifying the options with the given conditions is the fastest method.

**Condition 1:** 3 years ago, the person's age was 6 × his brother's age.

Checking Option 1 (15 years, 5 years): Ages 3 years ago were 12 and 2. Since 12 = 6 × 2, it is true.

**Condition 2:** 8 years later, person's age will be 2 × brother's age − 3.

Ages 8 years later will be 23 and 13. Since 23 = 2 × 13 − 3 = 26 − 3, it is also true.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years and 5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8438908b9ffabfd8f69a1a8b4350c3f59db43bbe3ec606b1b06f057915f84ec3.png] 

Let the present age of the person be P and his younger brother be B.

**Step 1: Applying the condition for 3 years ago**

⇒ P − 3 = 6 × (B − 3)

⇒ P − 3 = 6B − 18

⇒ P − 6B = −15 ... (Equation 1)

**Step 2: Applying the condition for 8 years later**

⇒ P + 8 = 2 × (B + 8) − 3

⇒ P + 8 = 2B + 16 − 3

⇒ P − 2B = 5 ... (Equation 2)

**Step 3: Solving the linear equations**

Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ (P − 2B) − (P − 6B) = 5 − (−15)

⇒ 4B = 20

⇒ B = 5

Substitute B = 5 in Equation 2:

⇒ P − 2(5) = 5

⇒ P − 10 = 5

⇒ P = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years and 5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Present Age Variable Assumption

It is always best to assume the current age as the variable (like x). This way, age 't' years ago becomes (x − t) and age 't' years later easily becomes (x + t) without any confusion.

Constant Age Difference Concept

The difference between the ages of two individuals always remains constant at any point in time. If a person is 5 years older than their brother today, they will always remain 5 years older.

Cross-Multiplication Method

When solving age problems given in ratios over two different time periods, we can equate the cross-product differences of the ratios to the difference in the given time intervals directly.
